title: B200 capacity & driver/CUDA standardization plan (Infra memo)
body:
Owner: Irene Choi (Infra)
Reviewed with: Neha Kapoor, Vanessa Ortiz
Last reviewed in infra sync: 2026-02-18

Purpose
- Document expected B200 fleet timeline + capacity shape (Hosted + Dedicated)
- Define the driver/CUDA “standard baseline” we will target for B200 bring-up in Q1/Q2 2026
- Enumerate the variance that *will* exist (and for how long), and what variance must be handled by the runtime Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack (compatibility checks + safe defaults)

This memo is intended to unblock:
- Runtime profile pack gating (B200 compatibility gate)
- SRE rollout guardrails (what constitutes a “bad node” vs “expected variance”)
- Release engineering expectations for runtime-1.22 / profile pack launch


Summary (TL;DR)
- Capacity: expect a small, heterogeneous B200 canary fleet in late Feb–Mar; meaningful capacity ramps in Apr–May; region-by-region variance is expected through at least mid-Q2.
- Baseline decision (B200 “standard”): NVIDIA driver 550.54.14 + CUDA 12.4 runtime images for initial bring-up.
- Exceptions: we will temporarily allow a small number of nodes on 550.90.xx (vendor preload) and a very small number on 555.x in a lab setting only.
- Profiles must handle:
  - Driver minor-version spread (within 550.x) without silent behavior changes; runtime should surface an explicit compatibility result.
  - SXM vs PCIe differences (power/clock behavior) in performance expectations; we should treat them as separate “hardware variants” where feasible.
  - Early firmware/VBIOS variance (watch for kernel fallback rate and instability counters).
- Policy: Hosted will only run “supported baseline combos”; Dedicated/Private can run outside baseline but must require explicit profile pin + noisy warnings (and ideally refusal for known-unsafe combos).


1) Context
We are onboarding B200 as a near-future SKU alongside H100 and L40S. The runtime project (Hardware tuning profiles pack) is adding:
- SKU detection + compatibility gate (see redwood/pr-24927)
- Per-SKU defaults and versioned profile selection

Infra’s role is to:
- Standardize the host stack (driver/CUDA/OS/firmware) as early as possible
- Provide a compatibility matrix + migration plan so Runtime can implement deterministic selection rules and guardrails


2) Capacity timeline (forecast, subject to change)
Notes:
- “Nodes” refers to physical hosts / instances in Redwood-controlled fleet.
- Regions are illustrative; actual placement depends on datacenter/vendor deliveries.

Milestone table
- Week of 2026-02-17: 2–4 B200 nodes in benchmark-lab only (bring-up + smoke)
- Week of 2026-02-24: 6–10 nodes in one primary region (Hosted canary + benchmark-lab)
- Week of 2026-03-10: 20–30 nodes total across 2 regions (Hosted opt-in + limited Dedicated pilots)
- Week of 2026-04-07: 60–90 nodes total across 3 regions (Dedicated general pilots; Hosted gradual expansion)
- Week of 2026-05-05: 150–250 nodes total (depending on delivery + power/cooling constraints)

Constraints that may move dates:
- Vendor lead times and rack power approvals
- Firmware validation loop (VBIOS/board firmware)
- Kernel/driver regressions discovered via runtime profile canary


3) Host + container baseline (what we will standardize)
3.1 OS baseline
- Host OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- Host kernel: 6.5.x (align with current H100 fleet standard)
- Container runtime: containerd

Rationale:
- Matches existing fleet operational model (patch cadence, monitoring, tooling).

3.2 Driver baseline (initial bring-up)
Baseline for B200 production (Hosted + Dedicated):
- NVIDIA driver: 550.54.14

Allowed temporary variance (time-boxed):
- 550.90.xx: allowed for vendor-preloaded nodes for up to 4 weeks, provided smoke + perf canary passes and runtime does not observe elevated kernel fallbacks.
- 555.x: benchmark-lab only until we explicitly bless it (no Hosted/Dedicated traffic).

Non-allowed:
- < 550.54.14 on B200 (we will not route any prod traffic; runtime should refuse by default).

Why 550.54.14?
- Most stable option we have validated internally on early nodes.
- Lowest-risk starting point to reduce confounding variables during kernel + scheduler tuning.

3.3 CUDA baseline (container images)
Baseline runtime image for bring-up:
- CUDA 12.4

Notes:
- We expect to evaluate CUDA 12.5 once:
  1) Benchmark-lab results are stable (week-over-week) and
  2) kernel fallback counters remain low under the profile defaults

Operational policy:
- We aim to keep CUDA version changes behind runtime release trains, not ad-hoc per region.


4) Known sources of variance (and how we plan to handle them)
We should assume the B200 fleet will not be perfectly uniform in Q1–early Q2. Key variances:

4.1 Driver minor versions (550.54 vs 550.90)
- Expectation: Some early nodes ship with 550.90.xx preinstalled.
- Plan: Infra will re-image to 550.54.14 where feasible; exceptions allowed short-term.
- Requirement for runtime profile pack:
  - Explicit compatibility matrix keyed by (sku, driver_major.minor, cuda_major.minor)
  - Runtime must emit “compatibility decision” as a first-class signal (supported / warn / refuse)

4.2 SXM vs PCIe form factor
- Expectation: We may receive mixed form factors depending on vendor supply.
- Impact:
  - Different power/clock behavior; can shift throughput and tail latency characteristics.
- Plan:
  - Infra exposes form factor as hardware metadata if available.
  - If we cannot reliably surface this in time, the runtime should treat observed performance variance as expected and rely on guardrails (admission control, queue limits) rather than aggressive batching.

4.3 Firmware / VBIOS versions
- Expectation: Early shipments may include different firmware revs.
- Plan:
  - Track firmware versions in inventory and correlate with runtime’s kernel fallback + error counters.
- Requirement for runtime profile pack:
  - Treat elevated kernel fallback rate as “suspect node” signal; do not auto-expand canary if correlated.

4.4 Interconnect / topology differences (PCIe gen, NUMA)
- Expectation: Host CPU + NUMA layouts may differ in early fleet.
- Plan:
  - Prefer a single reference server SKU; but don’t block early bring-up.
- Requirement for profiles:
  - Profiles should include safe defaults for CPU pinning and NUMA guidance as “best-effort” (especially for Private installs).


5) What variance must be handled by the tuning profiles pack
This section is the contract we need Runtime to implement (or explicitly reject).

5.1 Compatibility gates
The runtime should compute:
- detected_sku (B200)
- driver_version
- cuda_version (runtime image)
- profile_version + profile_id

And enforce:
- Hosted: only (B200 + 550.54.14 + CUDA 12.4) as “supported” for initial rollout
- Dedicated: allow “warn” state for 550.90.xx if perf-canary says OK; require explicit customer pin for anything outside “supported”
- Private: allow warn/refuse with strong messaging; never silently accept a “refuse” combo

Suggested policy states (shared language across Infra/SRE/Runtime):
- SUPPORTED: OK for default selection (no operator action)
- WARN: run allowed but must log + export metric + surface in /health; requires opt-in in Hosted (or explicit pin outside Hosted)
- REFUSE: runtime should fail fast unless “override_unsafe=true” is set (Private only) and should still emit very loud warnings

5.2 Deterministic profile selection
- If B200 + supported baseline: select default B200 profile for the workload bucket.
- If B200 + warn baseline: either
  - select a conservative B200 profile variant (lower concurrency / more headroom), or
  - require explicit profile pin (preferred for Hosted; acceptable for Dedicated)

5.3 Observability
Infra needs the following metrics to debug fleet variance:
- kernel_choice / kernel_fallback counters tagged by (sku, profile_id, driver)
- scheduler_queue_ms and request queue depth
- OOM + fragmentation counters (especially if the default headroom is wrong)


6) Rollout expectations (Infra + SRE coordination)
- Benchmark-lab is the first gate: B200 nodes must run the minimal matrix (smoke) before any Hosted canary traffic.
- Hosted canary cohorts should be constrained:
  - single region, low % of traffic, known model set
  - limit to supported baseline combos

SRE asks (aligning with Sean/Rafael):
- Kill-switch must be available to revert to “no profile pack” behavior or last-known-good profile version.
- If we see elevated p99/p999 + kernel fallbacks: pause expansion and re-image outlier nodes first before retuning knobs.


7) Action items / owners
Infra (Irene / Vanessa)
- [ ] Maintain inventory list for B200 nodes: (region, form factor, driver, firmware)
- [ ] Re-image vendor-preloaded 550.90.xx nodes to 550.54.14 where feasible
- [ ] Publish “B200 baseline status” in weekly infra update (count supported vs warn)

Runtime (Noah / Yuki / Quentin)
- [ ] Implement compatibility matrix + policy states (supported/warn/refuse)
- [ ] Ensure profile selection is deterministic and logged at startup/model load

SRE (Sean / Rafael)
- [ ] Define canary gating thresholds specifically for B200 bring-up (kernel fallback rate thresholds TBD)

Release Eng (Connor)
- [ ] Make driver/CUDA baseline a release checklist item for runtime-1.22 enablement


8) Open questions
- Do we have reliable telemetry for B200 form factor (SXM vs PCIe) in the current hardware metadata pipeline?
- What is our target date to bless 555.x + CUDA 12.5 (if perf improvements materialize)?
- Should we treat “driver minor version drift within 550.x” as WARN by default until we’ve collected enough canary data?


Appendix A: Proposed compatibility matrix (initial)
- B200 + Driver 550.54.14 + CUDA 12.4 => SUPPORTED
- B200 + Driver 550.90.xx + CUDA 12.4 => WARN (time-boxed; Hosted opt-in only)
- B200 + Driver 555.x + CUDA 12.4/12.5 => REFUSE for prod (benchmark-lab only until blessed)
- B200 + Driver < 550.54 => REFUSE

Appendix B: Notes from early bring-up
- Some early nodes show higher kernel fallback rates under long-context workloads; we suspect driver/firmware mismatch. Correlate fallback rate with firmware rev before changing kernel defaults.
- For now, treat “fallback rate spikes” as a fleet hygiene issue first (re-image / firmware update), not an auto-tuning problem.
